Marine Spatial Planning
In 2023 this subset of experts completed an ecological sensitivity 
analysis of the western Irish Sea. The reports and other outputs 
from this work are available through the following link: https://
www.gov.ie/en/publication/e00ec-marine-protected-areas/. 
That group have now been asked to undertake a follow-up 
ecological sensitivity analysis of the Celtic Sea. This is in order 
to identify, where possible, suitable areas within which Marine 
Protected Areas (MPAs) might be merited in the future under 
forthcoming legislation and associated processes. The work is 
also intended to inform future maritime management decisions 
in the region as relevant, including the spatial planning of sectoral 
activity, particularly relating to Offshore Renewable Energy (ORE). 
As per the Irish Sea study, the final report will be based on an 
analysis of the sensitivity of species, habitats and other ecological 
features to pressures arising from industrial activities in the 
region. The analyses will use objective procedures to identify 
suitable locations where such features could be given protection 
in the future, while seeking to minimise effects and costs to 
ongoing industry activity. 
As part of the stakeholder engagement and public participation 
plans the Environmental Assessment Officer attended the 
“Feature Selection Criteria” workshop held in Limerick on March 
25th. Input was provided via the workshop and roundtables 
discussions on feature selection across fish and invertebrates, 
non-Natura habitats and Ecosystem Services, Natura habitats 
and cetaceans together with Natura Bird. Key to the discussions 
was the availability of data and the lack of in some areas. 
However, there are >550 datasets available to or being ustilised 
by the National DMAP process and both it and this process 
overlap therefore the bank of datasets will be used to inform the 
ecological sensitivity analysis. Key for Clare County Council is the 
Shannon Estuary and its importance as an ecologically sensitive 
ecosystem. Marine Protected Areas could stretch up into an 
estuary or transitional waters if a “feature” is present highlighting 
the importance of making any data available for the Shannon 
Estuary to the study.

the county’s Stained Glass heritage was launched. The archive 
was created by West Clare based researcher and photographer 
John Glynn. This brings together over five years of research into 
stained glass windows from more than 130 religious and secular 
sites. 
The project highlights a significant yet often under recognised 
aspect of Clare’s cultural heritage, spanning seven centuries from 
the 14th century to the present day. The archive documents 
over 1,000 images of stained-glass windows and their buildings, 
alongside detailed information including location, Eircode, GPS 
coordinates, and history. Each window has its own description 
and high-quality image with a summary of its title, location, 
studio, inscriptions and donors. The archive includes Bunratty 
Castle, home to over 100 medieval and pre 19th century-stained 
glass windows sourced from England, Switzerland, Germany and 
the Benelux region.
The project is supported by The Irish Community Archive Network 
(iCAN) at the National Museum of Ireland, The Heritage Council 
and Clare County Council Heritage Officer. Learn more: https://

National Heritage Week 2026 
National Heritage Week 2026 will take place from 15th - 23rd 
August. Included in this will be Heritage Open Doors on 15th/16th 
August, Wild Child Day on 22nd August and Water Heritage Day 
on 23rd August. 
The theme for National Heritage Week 2026 is “Heritage at Risk”.
This theme will highlight the natural, built, and cultural heritage 
endangered in Ireland. From habitats to cultural practices to 
heritage sites, we are encouraging event organisers to explore 
the theme through exploring and sharing the stories of heritage 
at risk in their locality. You can read more about the theme here:

North Munster Artificial Lighting Workshop for 
Council Staff
On Wednesday 15th of April, the Biodiversity Officers of Clare, 
Tipperary, Limerick and Kerry organised a one-day training 
workshop on the responsible use of artificial lighting and lighting 
design aimed at Council Staff (planners, engineers, architects and 
other technical staff) to benefit wildlife. Guest speakers included 
Catherine Casey (Head of Climate, Heritage Council), Peter 
McLoughlin (Mayo County Council), Kerem Asfuroglu (Lighting 
Consultant and Designer, Dark Sources), Georgia MacMillan 
(Mayo Dark Sky) and Dr. Tina Aughney (Bat Ecoservices). The 
workshop investigated different ways how we can reduce our 
impact associated with light pollution such as adopting warm 
colour temperature lighting (orange) and retrofitting public 
lighting which is bat and wildlife-friendly, avoiding the installation 
of lighting along rivers, hedgerows and woodlands (which 
impacts negatively on wildlife), avoiding lighting up buildings 
and monuments or alternatively reducing artificial light intensity. 
More communities in Clare are embracing the Dark Sky initiative 
which ties in with actions for Tidy Towns, Community Biodiversity 
Action Plans and promoting best practice.

Project Development Measure - Sixmilebridge
The Project Development Measure aims to improve safe, 
accessible, and inclusive pedestrian movement across the 
O’Garney River while enhancing the town centre public realm. 
Survey work for a proposed new pedestrian footbridge identified 
significant constraints, prompting the consideration of alternative 
solutions in consultation with the Sixmilebridge Town Team.
In late 2025, a signalised traffic management solution for the 
existing bridge was identified, surveyed, and tested. Findings 
confirm that the bridge cannot safely accommodate two-way 
vehicular traffic alongside pedestrians; however, a signal-
controlled single-lane system enables safer, more controlled 
vehicle movements while prioritising pedestrian access.
This revised approach maintains the original project objectives 
through a “pedestrian first, vehicles second” framework, 
allowing for the rationalisation of vehicular space and the 
delivery of enhanced, high-quality pedestrian and public realm 
improvements, ensuring accessibility and inclusivity for all users.

Healthy Ireland Framework consultation:
THE Department of Health conducted a public consultation on a 
new Healthy Ireland Framework inviting people to have their say 
in helping to shape the future direction of health and wellbeing 
policy in Ireland. The consultation was open until 22nd April. 
Supported by the Healthy Ireland team in Clare County Council 
and the Healthy Clare Working Group; individuals, communities 
and organisations across the County were encouraged to engage 
with the consultation as any new Framework will have impacts 
for County Clare. The new framework will help guide national 
policy and action to improve health outcomes and reduce health 
inequalities over the coming years.

the Department of Health and covers Healthy Ireland projects 
and a Healthy Ireland Co-ordinator. By the end of 2026, the 
Department of Health will have contributed €719k towards the 
Healthy Ireland Fund for County Clare between 2022 and 2026. 
This funding assists the implementation of a four-year strategy

Framework. Finance and Progress Reports for 2025 have been

Bealtaine Art Expo - 16th April 26 in the Temple

The Bealtaine Art Expo took place today at the Temple Gate Hotel, 
Ennis, celebrating the creativity of older people across County 
Clare. The exhibition showcased a vibrant collection of artworks 
created by clients of Clarecastle Day Care Centre, Carrigoran Day 
Care Centre, Raheen Day Care Centre, the Community Nursing 
Unit, and Ennistymon Community Hospital. The event ran from 
10:00 am to 4:00 pm, with a well-attended evening viewing held 
from 6:00 pm to 8:00 pm. Admission was free, encouraging the 
public to engage with and enjoy the diverse range of artistic pieces 
on display. As part of the Bealtaine Festival, selected artworks 
from the expo will also be exhibited throughout May in libraries 
across Ennis, Shannon, Scariff, and Ennistymon, ensuring wider 
community access to the work and continuing the celebration of 
creativity in later life.

Road Safety for Older People - 18th April in Clare 
Marts 
A free Road Safety and Information and Demonstration Event for 
older road users was held on Saturday, 18 April 2026, from 2:00 
pm to 4:00 pm at Clare Marts, Quin Road, Ennis. The event was 
organised by the Clare Older People’s Council in partnership with 
Clare County Council’s Age Friendly Programme. The afternoon 
featured practical demonstrations and advice on safe driving, 
roundabout use, and road safety for motorists, pedestrians, 
and cyclists. An Garda Síochána attended alongside the Local 
Community Safety Partnership, providing a property marking 
service and crime prevention advice. RSA driving instructor Chris 
Quin was also present, offering guidance to road users on safe 
and confident driving. Keith Whyte of Pat Foudy & Daughter 
carried out complimentary tyre checks for car and van owners, 
while Clare Fire Brigade personnel engaged with attendees, 
providing advice on fire service procedures and what to expect 
during a road traffic accident. The event was well attended and 
provided a valuable opportunity for older road users to access 
expert advice, practical supports, and safety information in a 
welcoming and accessible setting.

Manager Shanelle Waring met with the Harmony Ladies Group to 
deliver an informative presentation on Ageing in Place, available 
home adaptation grants, and the key priorities of the Clare Age 
Friendly County Strategy 2024 - 2030.During the session, Shanelle 
discussed how the strategy is designed to support older people 
to live independently in their own homes and communities for 
as long as possible. She outlined initiatives that promote safety, 
accessibility, and social inclusion, alongside the practical supports 
available to help older adults plan positively for later life.
The presentation also created an opportunity for open discussion, 
with members sharing their experiences and raising questions 
about local issues affecting older people. This engagement 
reflects the Clare Age Friendly Programme’s ongoing commitment 
to listening to older people and ensuring their voices inform the 
implementation and delivery of the Age Friendly Strategy across 
the county.

being to bring together our resources with a strong ambition for

DERELICT SITES

across the County is underway with 380 derelict properties 
being dealt with by the Derelict Sites Team as of the 20th April

in the last month. The team maintains very high levels of 
activity and engagement with owners and their legal/technical 
representatives. This initial engagement is key to resolution of 
the issues of dereliction and to gain an understanding of the 
various reasons why the properties are in a derelict state. Where 
derelict properties are sold by the owner, the Derelict Sites Team 
engages promptly with the new owners to brief them on their 
responsibilities under the Derelict Sites Act, 1990. 
To bolster the momentum, the Council is advising property 
owners on accessing the vacant property refurbishment grant 
and the recently announced grants for commercial premises and 
over-the-shop opportunities. The Team is also seeing a consistent 
number of planning applications for property refurbishment/
extensions, and it is clear from driving around the county the 
level of work ongoing on individual properties. The Derelict Sites 
Team believe that by working in partnership with owners and 
financial institutions, there are real opportunities for the positive

Working Together to Bring Properties Back to Life
The Derelict Sites Section is committed to supporting and guiding 
property owners. Assistance is available to help identify practical 
solutions, access relevant schemes/grants and navigate the 
steps required to bring properties back into habitable use. The 
importance of timely action by the owner cannot be overstated. 
In parallel, owners are advised that the provisions of the Derelict 
Sites Act 1990 will be applied where necessary. This may result 
in a property being entered on the Derelict Sites Register, 
the imposition of a 7% annual levy, and/or consideration for 
compulsory purchase. By engaging early and taking proactive 
steps - through refurbishment, redevelopment or reuse - owners 
can reduce potential levy liabilities while making a positive 
contribution to the appearance and wellbeing of their community.
From Dereliction to Opportunity
Revitalising derelict and neglected properties is about far more 
than visual improvement - it is about unlocking the full potential 
of our communities. Clare County Council’s Derelict Sites Team are 
leading this transformation with renewed focus, determination 
and a strong commitment to applying the Derelict Sites Act 1990 
to its full extent.
Derelict and neglected buildings have long had a detrimental 
impact on the character, vitality and liveability of our towns, 
villages and rural hinterlands. Through a targeted, proactive 
and systematic approach, Clare County Council is addressing 
this challenge head-on. The number of properties actively 
being progressed under derelict sites legislation has increased 
significantly, rising from 303 at the end of 2025 to 380 today,

area increasing to €53m in 2025.
